question.text: Famous Tang poet Li Bai was born in a town along this trading route from China to the Mediterranean. A particular Chinese fabric gave this trading route its name.
question.clue: In the plural, this term was subtitled A New History of the World in a work by Peter Frankopan, and it names Yo-Yo Ma's ensemble to promote cross-cultural artistic collaboration.

swap.leadin: This man was born near Lake Baikal with the name Temujin ("TEH-moo-jin").
swap.text: Name this man who was proclaimed "universal ruler" in a 1206 assembly.
swap.clue: A "Secret History" describes his childhood under the name Temujin (TEH-mue-jeen).

question.leadin: Following this man's brutal sack of Baghdad, he had human skulls stacked into giant pyramids.
question.text: Name this famously handicapped Central Asian conqueror of Mongol origin who conquered a massive empire before suddenly dying en route to an invasion of China.
question.clue: This man destroyed Sarai after winning the Battle of Terek River against his former ally Tokhtamysh.

swap.leadin: Answer some things about the foreign policy of George W. Bush.
swap.text: Following the 9/11 attacks, the United States invaded Afghanistan in order to overthrow this political group which controlled the country and harbored Al Qaeda.
swap.clue: This group, the main opponent of the Northern Alliance, carried out the "green on blue" attacks.

question.text: The An Lushan Rebellion forced the Tang to retreat from its Western Protectorate, which would later be conquered by an empire named for this region governed from Lhasa.
question.clue: Gushi Khan later supported the establishment of the Ganden Phodrang, which was ruled by Ngawang Lobsang Gyatso.

swap.leadin: This polity's founder Batu expanded its frontiers into Hungary by winning the Battle of Mohi over Bela IV in 1241.
swap.text: Name this polity which ruled Russia and Eastern Europe in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries and splintered after being crippled by the Timurids.
swap.clue: This state lost control of one city to Grand Duke Algirdas after its defeat at the Battle of Blue Waters.

question.text: At another Battle of Bach Dang River, a Tran-dynasty general defeated an invasion from this group of people, who were at the time led by Genghis Khan's grandson, Kublai.
question.clue: The Russian Empire committed genocide against the Buryat and Kalmyk variant of these people, and they were once ruled by the Austrian adventurer Baron Ungern.

swap.leadin: Military councils known as kurultai elected this polity's leaders, who included Ogedei and Mongke.
swap.text: Identify this polity formed in 1206 when Temujin was proclaimed Genghis Khan.
swap.clue: It used a trebuchet to beat the Southern Song at Xiangyang .

question.leadin: In 1839, the British deposed the king of this territory and replaced him with a puppet ruler.
question.text: Identify this modern-day country that ceded territory via the Treaty of Gandamak to British. Britain initially got involved in this country after an attack on its city of Herat.
question.clue: A Soviet invasion saw the U.S. support the Islamic Mujahideen, and a subsequent civil war that led to the rise of the Taliban.

swap.leadin: Qazi ("kah-zi") Mullah led a state in this mountain range that was invaded during the Murid War.
swap.text: Name this mountain range, where the Naqshbandi Sufi leader Imam Shamil led resistance to foreign occupation. The Circassian ethnic group is from this mountain range.
swap.clue: Gold and silver tubes, possibly used to drink beer, that were found in this region were made by the Maykop culture, which, like this region's Kura-Araxes culture, constructed burial mounds called kurgans.

question.leadin: This country's three largest tribes are called juz and were descended from the mythical figure Alash.
question.text: Name this present-day country that briefly changed its capital's name to honor Nursaltan Nazarbayev, who led this country after it was the last to break away from the Soviet Union.
question.clue: It was the last Soviet Republic to declare its independence, doing so in December of 1991.

swap.text: The European Union suspended most diplomatic relations with Uzbekistan following the May 2005 incident in this city, where demonstrators were massacred by the army in Bobur Square after twenty-three accused terrorists broke out of prison.

question.text: The Ballad of Mulan instead depicts her fighting the Rouran ("roh-rahn"), who are the first historical people of note to use this title for their rulers. This Turkic title was also given to the leader of the Mongols.
question.clue: One of these figures destroyed the Khwarezmian cities of Urgench and Samarkand and established his capital at Karakorum.

swap.leadin: A vizier of an empire whose capital was this city may have been a secret Manichaean.
swap.text: Name this city, the capital of the Samanid Empire whose rulers commissioned Ferdowsi to write the Shahnameh. Alongside the Khanate of Khiva, an emirate ruled from this city later became a Russian protectorate.
swap.clue: A group modelled off the Young Turks invited the Soviet conquest of this city and was given prominent leadership positions in the short-lived Soviet republic centered on this city.

question.leadin: An article by Malcolm Yapp claims that this historical importance of this conflict was artificially inflated.
question.text: Name this term that denotes the strategic rivalry between Great Britain and Russia for control over Central Asia between 1813 to 1907.
question.answerHtml: The Great Game [or Tournament of Shadows; or Turniry Teney]
question.clue: The Fortress of Orenburg was constructed in order to control the Kazakhs as part of this period, which also saw extended maneuvering over the rights to Sinkiang.

swap.text: Once the Red Army toppled Ungern von Sternberg, this early Mongolian leader liquidated Mongolian Buddhist institutions and clergy after pushing out Peljidiin Genden, who had denied Stalin's requests to do so.
swap.clue: With Shtern and Zukhov, this man commanded the winning side at the Battle of Khalkin Gol.

question.text: The author of History of the Hind, al-Biruni, traveled to India with the invading forces of Mahmud-i Zabuli, the first Sultan of this Turkic empire which broke off from the Samanids.
question.answerHtml: the Ghaznavid Empire [or Ghaznaviyan; Mahmud’s father Sabuktigin founded the dynasty but Mahmud was the first to call it a Sultanate]
question.clue: This empire whose first leader, Sabuktigin, was a slave before being promoted by Alptigin.

swap.leadin: According to some tales, this tribe was founded by the son of a wolf, who also appears in the Epic of Ergenekon.
swap.text: Name this Turkic tribe. This tribe's leader Bumin rebelled against the Rouran Confederation and founded the First Turkic Empire, which was led by this ruling clan of the Gokturks.

question.leadin: Boris Yeltsin once got so drunk that at a 1992 state dinner, he took a pair of wooden spoons and began drumming a tune on this leader's bald head.
question.text: Name this Central Asian leader, whose son Aidar married Nursultan Nazarbayev's daughter Aliya. The youth movement KelKel opposed this distinctively-eyebrowed, corrupt authoritarian, and helped pressure his resignation in 2005 during the Tulip Revolution.

swap.text: Yakub Beg's state is commonly named after this city, his capital and most important of the seven "Yettishahr" cities. This city in the far west of the Tarim Basin has long been an important hub for trade across the Pamirs.
swap.clue: This city was the capital of the Shule ("shu-luh") Kingdom.
